title: Thirty years of radioshack.com
lede: These are screenshots of the Internet Archive’s captures of radioshack.com, stored as images; click one to open the original capture. The front page tracks the company’s identity: parts, then partners, then phones, then a liquidation, a crypto token and a web shop.[^33]
note: Screenshots of Internet Archive captures, saved as images; click one to open the original capture. Later captures show the afterlife: a clearance store in [Jul 2017](https://web.archive.org/web/20170701003943/http://www.radioshack.com/), a crypto waitlist in [Jan 2022](https://web.archive.org/web/20220101093831/https://www.radioshack.com/) and a conventional shop under Unicomer in [Apr 2025](https://web.archive.org/web/20250401012431/https://www.radioshack.com/).

captures.label: The first storefront
captures.title: The first storefront
captures.text: A corporate brochure more than a shop: a big round logo over a tiled background, buttons for Store Locator, Future Activities, Contacts, Press Releases and History & Info, and links to “Steve’s Workbench,” a hobbyist help page, and the company’s “United Against Crime” program.

captures.label: Parts, partners and gifts
captures.title: Parts, partners and gifts
captures.text: The first real catalog, at the height of the company’s profits. The left column lists the parts business; the partner logos say where management was looking: computers, satellite TV and phones.

captures.label: The phone store
captures.title: The phone store
captures.text: The year sales peaked at $5.08B. The home page leads with “Now you can buy wireless online!” and a carrier-plan picker. Parts and accessories sit in the left-hand category list.

captures.label: The last redesign
captures.title: The last redesign
captures.text: Three months before Chapter 11. A modern, photo-led site built around “projects” and “services,” the company’s pitch to makers and to people who needed help with their phones.
